title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 60 (Application of payment where debt to be discharged is not indicated)

content.overview: Section 60 provides that where the debtor has omitted to intimate and there are no other circumstances indicating to which debt the payment is to be applied, the creditor may apply it at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable to him from the debtor, whether its recovery is or is not barred by the law in force for the time being as to the limitation of suits.
content.glance: No indication by debtor → creditor may apply payment to any lawful debt actually due (including time-barred); not to disputed or unlawful debt.
content.study: Where the debtor has not indicated the debt and circumstances do not indicate application, the creditor may apply the payment at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable, whether or not recovery is barred by limitation. Current-law framing: confirm absence of indication; apply creditor’s discretion to any lawful debt actually due (including time-barred).

sections.heading: Creditor’s discretion
sections.body: Creditor may apply the payment at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable, whether or not barred by limitation.

provisions.title: Application of payment where debt to be discharged is not indicated

examples.title: No indication
examples.body: A owes B several debts and pays a sum without indicating which. B may apply it to any lawful debt actually due, including one barred by limitation, under s. 60.

hypotheticals.question: Can the creditor apply an unindicated payment to a time-barred debt?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 60 allows application to any lawful debt actually due, whether or not recovery is barred by limitation.

misconceptions.trap: The creditor can never apply a payment to a time-barred debt.
misconceptions.correction: Section 60 expressly allows application to a lawful debt actually due even if barred by limitation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 60 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm no indication by debtor. II. Apply creditor’s discretion to any lawful debt actually due. III. Note limitation does not bar application. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State creditor’s discretion and the limitation point.
